R1.required_action: remain U; replay only the same cas1 p→c with identical (p,slice_id)

R2.required_action: recover C; do not replay cas1; next eligible mutation is only cas2 c→a
R2.bug_falsified: duplicate certificate generation/write after accepted-no-ack cas1

R3.required_action: recover terminal A; do not emit any additional ADVANCE
R3.bug_falsified: requiring an observed intermediate S before recognizing the exact same lineage already advanced

R4.required_action: enter terminal F; no cas1 or cas2 replay for this lineage
R4.bug_falsified: misclassifying an unrelated descendant as own progress

R5.required_action: remain C; replay only the same cas2 c→a
R5.bug_falsified: abandoning replay after a non-accepted or unobserved ADVANCE

R6.required_action: recover terminal A; suppress every further ADVANCE

R7.required_action: enter terminal F; suppress every further ADVANCE
R7.bug_falsified: overwriting or advancing through a conflicting descendant

R8.required_action: enter terminal F as lineage regression/stale-invalid observation; do not replay cas1 or cas2 from C
R8.bug_falsified: rolling a committed certificate lineage backward to U and creating a second logical attempt

bounded_leaf_result.minimality_argument: Relative to the explicit decoder partition {stage after cas1 ambiguity, stage after cas2 ambiguity} × {P,S,exact-A,other-O}, all eight rows are required for a total adversarial checker. Stage changes the legal replay predecessor: P means cas1 replay only in U but is a regression in C; S means recovery to C after cas1 ambiguity but cas2 replay after cas2 ambiguity. Exact-A must be recognized at either stage to recover accepted progress, while O must fence at either stage. Removing any row leaves at least one stage/observation class untested and permits an implementation that is correct on the remaining rows but unsafe or non-live on the omitted class.

duplicate_advance_safety_proof.invariant: cas2 is legal only from state C when the current repository value is exactly c and it always targets the single deterministic a for the same (p,slice_id,c).
duplicate_advance_safety_proof.proof: At most one successful cas2 can consume c because repository CAS requires c to be current. After any successful c→a or any conflicting replacement of c, c is no longer current, so a second c→a CAS cannot succeed. R6 terminates on exact a, R7 fences on other descendant, and R8 fences regression. R5 may retry only the same deterministic cas2 while c remains current, so acknowledgement loss cannot create a second logical ADVANCE identity.
duplicate_advance_safety_proof.scope_limit: This proves duplicate-ADVANCE suppression only for the repository state transition. It does not prove exactly-once behavior for any external side effect that might later be coupled to ADVANCE.

assumptions: Repository reads/CAS are eventually available across invocations; same-run waiting is not required.
Reads used for acceptance are exact current-value observations, not unvalidated stale caches.
No permanent conflicting writer replaces the lineage value; conflicts correctly terminate in F rather than being hidden.
Retries reuse the same p, c, a, and slice_id identities.
replay_liveness_proof.proof: If cas1 was not accepted, eventual P permits the same cas1 retry; if cas1 was accepted without acknowledgement, eventual S recovers C, or exact A recovers terminal success if the same lineage already advanced. From C, if cas2 was not accepted, eventual S permits the same cas2 retry; if cas2 was accepted without acknowledgement, eventual exact A recovers terminal success. Therefore acknowledgement loss alone cannot strand a non-conflicting lineage: the same identities reconstruct the next legal action across runs.
replay_liveness_proof.quota_rate_limit_note: Temporary connector/rate-limit unavailability may delay a retry to a later invocation but is not a finite monthly/trial/paid quota dependency and does not justify same-run polling.
